sentences.text: 2] Both the sides are heard.

2 913-Cri.Appln. 5607-2013.o 3] The crime is registered on the basis of report given by one Smt. 
Sawant who is working as the Food Safety Officer, under the aforesaid special enactment.
On 20.09.2013 at about 5.30 p.m. she inspected Balaji Pan Center of Sonpeth to ascertain as to whether Gutkha which was banned in the State was kept there.
In the search, she recovered five packets of Goa gutkha containing 60 pouch each.
This gutkha was taken over by her.
Manik More was present in the shop.
After seizure, she gave report to the Police and crime came to be registered.

4] The learned counsel for the applicant mainly submitted that in view of the provisions of aforesaid Special Enactment the crime could not have been registered and the prosecution ought to have been launched by Food Safety Officer by filing complaint before the learned Judicial Magistrate [F.C.].
He also submitted that the provisions of Indian Penal Code mentioned above cannot be used as special enactment is made to take action when food article is involved in the matter.
5] There is no force in both the aforesaid submissions made for the applicant.
This point was considered by the Apex Court in Criminal Application No. 1195 of 2018, ( The State of Maharashtra and others Vs. Sayyed Hasan and others) decided on 20.09.2018.

entities.text: State of Maharashtra and others Vs. Sayyed Hasan and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Apex Court has considered various provision of aforesaid special enactment and the 3 913-Cri.Appln. 5607-2013.odt
Apex Court has laid down that when offence punishable under Indian Penal Code is committed and it is cognizable in nature, crime can be registered.

The provision of Section 188 of the Indian Penal Code was considered, and it is laid down by the Apex Court that when there is prohibitory order and there is breach of the provision, Section 188 of the Indian Penal Code can be used.

The relevant provisions like Section 27 of the General Clauses Act are considered by the Apex Court and it is observed that there is no specific bar for registration of the crime in the scheme of the aforesaid special enactment.
This point was considered by this Court also in Writ Petition No. 3398 of 2011 ( Sanket Food Products Private Limited Vs. Union of Indian and others) with connected matters.

entities.text: Sanket Food Products Private Limited Vs. Union of Indian and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In that matter also Goa Gutkha was involved and this Court had considered the same challenges raised in the said matter.
In that case manufacturer was also involved.
In the present matter the vendor the person who was in found in possession of prohibited food articles is involved.
Thus, the provision of Section 273 of the Indian Penal Code involving the Food substances which is dangerous to the life can be used in the present matter.
The sample can be tested and ordinarily there is Magnesium Carbonate and there are also heavy metals in such substance.

This Court has considered the provision of the previous Act, The Food Adulteration Act and Rules framed there under and there is not much different in between those provisions and the provisions of new enactment.

It is laid down by this Manik Dhondiba More vs The State Of Maharashtra And Another on 3 October, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164561758/
2 Court that Guthkha is food and if 4 913-Cri.Appln. 5607-2013.odt it is sold ( as eatable) and the provisions of the Indian Penal Code like section 272 and 328 of the Indian Penal Code are applicable, the crime can be registered.

sentences.text: In the present matter also this Court hold that these provisions are squarely applicable and so the FIR cannot be quashed.
In the result the application stands dismissed.
